arxiv-1701-00931.title: Klein’s Fundamental 2-Form of Second Kind for the 𝑪 𝒂 ​ 𝒃 \boldsymbol{C_{ab}} Curves
arxiv-1701-00931.creator: Joe SUZUKI
arxiv-1701-00931.description: Abstract In this paper, we derive the exact formula of Klein’s fundamental 2-form of second kind for the so-called C a ​ b C_{ab} curves. The problem was initially solved by Klein in the 19th century for the hyper-elliptic curves, but little progress had been seen for its extension for more than 100 years.

arxiv-1801-10146.title: Star formation history from the cosmic infrared background anisotropies
arxiv-1801-10146.creator: A. Maniyar, M. Béthermin, G. Lagache
arxiv-1801-10146.description: Abstract We present a linear clustering model of cosmic infrared background (CIB) anisotropies at large scales that is used to measure the cosmic star formation rate density up to redshift 6, the effective bias of the CIB, and the mass of dark matter halos hosting dusty star-forming galaxies.

arxiv-2202-08099.title: Measuring Unintended Memorisation of Unique Private Features in Neural Networks
arxiv-2202-08099.creator: John Hartley, Sotirios A. Tsaftaris
arxiv-2202-08099.description: Abstract Neural networks pose a privacy risk to training data due to their propensity to memorise and leak information. Focusing on image classification, we show that neural networks also unintentionally memorise unique features even when they occur only once in training data. An example of a unique feature is a person’s name that is accidentally present on a training image.

arxiv-2205-14211.title: KL-Entropy-Regularized RL with a Generative Model is Minimax Optimal
arxiv-2205-14211.creator: Tadashi Kozuno 1, Wenhao Yang, Nino Vieillard, Toshinori Kitamura, Yunhao Tang, Jincheng Mei, Pierre Ménard, Mohammad Gheshlaghi Azar, Michal Valko, Rémi Munos, Olivier Pietquin, Matthieu Geist, Csaba Szepesvári
arxiv-2205-14211.description: Abstract In this work, we consider and analyze the sample complexity of model-free reinforcement learning with a generative model. Particularly, we analyze mirror descent value iteration (MDVI) by Geist et al. 2019 and Vieillard et al. 2020a , which uses the Kullback-Leibler divergence and entropy regularization in its value and policy updates.

arxiv-2206-13198.title: Constructing ‘full-frequency’ spectra via moment constraints for coupled cluster Green’s functions
arxiv-2206-13198.creator: Oliver J. Backhouse, George H. Booth
arxiv-2206-13198.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Oliver J. Backhouse, George H. Booth. We propose an approach to build ‘full-frequency’ quasiparticle spectra from conservation of a set of static expectation values. These expectation values define the moments of the spectral distribution, resulting in an efficient and systematically improvable expansion. By computing these initial moment constraints at the coupled-cluster level, we demonstrate convergence in both correlated state-specific and full spectral quantities, while requiring a fraction of the effort of traditional Green’s function approaches.

arxiv-2310-11109.title: MorphFlow: Estimating Motion in In Situ Tests of Concrete
arxiv-2310-11109.creator: Tessa Nogatz, Claudia Redenbach, Katja Schladitz
arxiv-2310-11109.description: Abstract We present a novel algorithm explicitly tailored to estimate motion from time series of 3D images of concrete. Such volumetric images are usually acquired by Computed Tomography and can contain for example in situ tests, or more complex procedures like self-healing. Our algorithm is specifically designed to tackle the challenge of large scale in situ investigations of concrete.

arxiv-2510-24132.description: Abstract This paper considers two closely related concepts, mixed Steiner system and nonuniform group divisible design (GDD). pmc-10572062.title: Increased Yearling Weight Gain Is Associated with a Distinct Faecal Microbial Profile
pmc-10572062.creator: Brianna N Maslen, Christian Duff, Samuel A Clark, Julius Van der Werf, Jason D White, Sameer D Pant, Mingliang Jin
pmc-10572062.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Simple SummaryGut microbial profiles have been shown to influence a range of physiological processes contributing to animal performance. In particular, gut microbiota have a close relationship with digestion and metabolism, indicating they may be correlated to weight gain. As previous studies have discussed, gut microbiota ranging from the rumen to the hindgut can influence and potentially indicate differences in important production traits such as milk composition in dairy cattle and feed efficiency in beef cattle.

pmc-12504519.title: A disaggregated system dynamics and agent-based modeling of the water-energy-food nexus for optimizing water allocation
pmc-12504519.creator: Soheila Zarei, Omid Bozorg-Haddad, Mohammad Reza Nikoo, Hugo A. Loáiciga
pmc-12504519.description: Asymmetric water distribution in agriculture is a significant threat to water, energy, and food security in water-limited areas. This work presents an integrated model framework based on System Dynamics and Agent-Based (SD-AB) modeling applying multi-objective evolutionary optimization with the non-dominated sorted genetic algorithm (NSGA)-II, and post-optimization analysis through Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) that facilitates sustainable water supply.

pmc-13421493.description: Androgenetic alopecia (AA) is a common condition that is characterized by androgen-induced follicular miniaturization and abnormal hair cycling, against which there are as yet no effective therapeutic interventions. The current study outlines the possibility of using stigmasterol (STR) as a therapeutic agent of AA, using geometry optimization, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations.
